_schema.owner: orchestrator (hand-maintained). tools/pack_textures.py READS this file and must never write it.
_schema.sets: Keys are texture sets from V2_CONTRACT section 5: parquet, marble, plaster, metal. An entry here overrides the procedural placeholder for that set.
_schema.channels: Paths are relative to _Museum/assets/. albedo = sRGB colour; normal_gl = OpenGL (+Y) normal; roughness / ao / metalness = single-channel greyscale; arm = pre-packed R=AO G=roughness B=metal (Poly Haven). A channel set to null is synthesised: ao=1.0, metalness=metal_default, roughness=roughness_default.
_schema.tile_m: Real-world size in metres covered by ONE repeat of the packed square texture (after square_mode). The materials module writes it into the slot materials' custom prop tile_m.
_schema.square_mode: How to make a non-square source square before resizing: 'none' (already square), 'stack' (repeat the source along its short axis until square; keeps aspect and stays seamless), 'crop' (centre crop).
_schema.albedo_mode: 'as_is' or 'neutralize' (divide the albedo by its mean colour and scale to the given target luminance, so tints come from baseColorFactor; used for the gold scan that serves gilt, brass and window_frame).
_schema.normal_strength: Scale of the normal's XY deviation (1.0 = unchanged, <1 flattens) before re-normalising.
_schema.roughness_scale / roughness_offset: Applied to the roughness channel: r' = clamp(r*scale + offset, 0.02, 1).

plaster._note: Source is 1024x512 (2:1). 'stack' repeats it vertically to 1024x1024, so one packed repeat = 3.0 m wide x 3.0 m tall containing two vertical source repeats. The scan has faint hairline cracks; normal_strength 0.5 keeps the wall calm.

metal._note: Gold scan; albedo neutralised so gilt (1.0 .78 .34), brass (.90 .70 .40) and window_frame (.22 .18 .14) tints come from baseColorFactor.
